This approach reduces the amount of re-rendering that occurs due to a user typing in an input...

claim: RHF docs concede that watch() re-renders at the root of the form/app and recommend useWatch to isolate re-rendering to the custom-hook level; useFormState is the analogous escape hatch for formState.

claim: react-final-form has effectively no field-level type inference: FieldProps defaults FieldValue to any, carries an unused _FormValues phantom, keeps `name: string` untyped, and adds an [key: string]: any index signature.
quote: export interface FieldProps<FieldValue = any, T = any, _FormValues = Record<string, any>> extends UseFieldConfig, Omit<RenderableProps<FieldRenderProps<FieldValue, T>>, "children"> { name: string; ... [key: string]: any; }

claim: react-final-form's only route to form-values typing is the withTypes<FormValues>() factory, which types Form/FormSpy but not Field.
quote: export declare function withTypes<FormValues = Record<string, any>>(): { Form: React.ComponentType<import("./types").FormProps<FormValues>>; FormSpy: React.ComponentType<import("./types").FormSpyProps<FormValues>>; };

claim: Expert critique of TanStack Form: because types come from defaultValues rather than the schema, optional fields and unions cannot express their full type range and still require manual casting plus a second source of truth.
quote: for optional fields or fields that start with no value at all, you need to provide a default that accurately represents the full range of valid types for that field, or the inference won't reflect it correctly

claim: Formik author Jared Palmer states publicly he has not maintained Formik since 2020; the 2.4.8 React 19 release was a Copilot dogfooding exercise, not a return to maintenance.
quote: Formik 2.4.8 is now available with React 19 support (long overdue ofc). I haven't maintained Formik since 2020, but it presents a wonderful playground to dogfood the latest @GitHub Copilot features, especially for some legit migrations.

claim: Formik collaborator johnrom tells the community to move to React Hook Form for new projects and says his planned Formik fork may never ship; existing Formik apps are 'unmaintained, not dangerous'.
quote: I would move on to React Hook Form if you're starting fresh. ... honestly I don't have much time to work on it and it wouldn't be released for a few months (if ever). ... If I can't spin up a fork with a better dev experience than RHF, then there's not really a point to release one.

claim: The only substantial Formik->RHF migration guide is Trussworks' (22 stars, last pushed 2023): it is a manual, form-by-form playbook with an API mapping table (<Formik/>->useForm(), <Field/>->register, useField()->useController(), useFormikContext()->useFormContext/useFormState/useWatch) and explicitly no codemod.
quote: Formik is unmaintained with the last version...published over 2 years ago... a maintainer of Formik has suggested not using Formik going forward, and instead recommends React Hook Form.

claim: The only official RHF codemod covers v6->v7 only (two transforms: v7/update-register and v7/move-errors-to-formState); latest release v1.2.1 from August 2021. No Formik->RHF codemod exists anywhere.
quote: Migrate React Hook Form V6 to V7 made simple. npx @hookform/codemod <transform> <path> [...options]

claim: LogRocket measures TanStack Form v1.11 at 9.6 KB gzip vs RHF v7.56 at 10.7 KB, and lands on RHF for simple forms, TanStack for complex ones, calling TanStack's field render-prop API materially more verbose.
quote: TanStack Form requires more code to set up than React Hook Form, especially in large applications... If you want to build a simple form with easy-to-use APIs but less verbosity, then React Hook Form is the go-to. But for more complex forms, TanStack Form will be a better and more comprehensive solution.

claim: HN commenter 'Escapado', shipping a form-heavy education SaaS, migrated RHF -> TanStack Form but reports TanStack Form's dirty-tracking breaks when default state changes and its type inference degrades on complex array types, forcing custom code.
quote: We started with react-hook-form and switched to Tanstack Form. ... Tanstack form is not meant for this (dirty tracking does not line up if the 'default state' changes) ... Tanstack form type inference for form fields is also lacking for complex array types for us.

claim: HN commenter describes the real-world Formik trap in 2026: an API they like, a codebase built around it, and a library that has fallen behind on performance and new React features with no real commits in years.
quote: I use a React form library called Formik. It's outdated and hasn't seen a real commit in years. The industry has moved onto other form libraries, but I really like Formik's api and have built quite a bit of functionality around it... it's lack of updates have caused it to fall behind in terms of performance and new React features.

claim: shadcn/ui shipped a form-library-agnostic <Field> component family in October 2025 supporting RHF, TanStack Form, React 19 useActionState and custom solutions — removing the biggest structural reason RHF was the default; in the same thread a commenter calls RHF outdated and is rebutted with the v8/React-Compiler work.
quote: By moving toward direct integration, shadcn becomes form-agnostic. You can use the exact same UI components whether you are an RHF fan or a TanStack Form enthusiast.

claim: shadcn/ui's canonical <Form> is still documented as a wrapper around react-hook-form, so the RHF-shaped ecosystem gravity remains even after the Field refactor.
quote: The <Form /> component is a wrapper around the react-hook-form library.

claim: Concrete criticism of Conform: it is coupled to Remix/Next server-action conventions, degrades in plain Vite+React where there is no server action, and is a poor fit for client-heavy multi-step wizards with cross-field state and live previews.
quote: Conform leans on Remix and Next.js conventions... in plain Vite + React the ergonomics suffer because there's no server action equivalent. Conform is less flexible for client-only complex forms — if you need a multi-step wizard with cross-field state and live previews, React Hook Form or TanStack Form give more knobs.

claim: Documented RHF type-soundness hole: a field typed number silently becomes a string on edit and TypeScript cannot catch it; the maintainer confirms it is unfixable at runtime and points to valueAsNumber as the workaround.
quote: the `score` value of type `number` got silently transformed as a `string` when I edit the field! ... [maintainer] There's no way to detect the input's `event.target.value` type passed into the form's value that's supposed to be a number at run-time in RHF as TS checks the types as when compiling

claim: The 'no form library' counter-reading (April 2026): RHF/Formik/TanStack all re-implement FormData and ValidityState in JS, tightly couple every input component to the library, and leave you stranded when it goes unmaintained (Redux Form as precedent); the author proposes form-associated custom elements + FormValidityObserver.
quote: Instead of using `FormData`, they re-create and manage the entire form's state in a separate JS object... instead of leveraging a field's ValidityState, they re-create and track their own error messages.

claim: 2026 aggregator verdict: RHF is the default for most React apps and works fine with React 19 server actions; Conform is the only library with first-class progressive enhancement; TanStack Form wins on nested/dynamic type inference; Formik is legacy/maintenance-mode.
quote: React Hook Form remains the default choice for most React applications in 2026 — battle-tested, performant, great ecosystem, and works well with React 19 server actions. ... By 2026, Formik is in maintenance mode — development has slowed significantly and the library hasn't adopted modern React patterns.

claim: TanStack Form's canonical React API is useForm({defaultValues, onSubmit}) plus a <form.Field name validators children={(field)=>...}> render prop with per-validator triggers (onChange/onChangeAsync/onBlur) and form.Subscribe for selective re-render — a render-prop model much closer to Formik's <Field> than to RHF's register().
quote: <form.Field name="firstName" validators={{ onChange: ({ value }) => !value ? 'A first name is required' : undefined }} children={(field) => (<input value={field.state.value} onBlur={field.handleBlur} onChange={(e) => field.handleChange(e.target.value)} />)} />

claim: Formisch (by Valibot author Fabian Hiller) is the 2026 new entrant — schema-first (useForm({schema}), <Field of={form} path={[...]}>) with types derived from one Valibot schema instead of a separate generic — but at 1,047 stars and ~2.5K weekly downloads it is not yet a production default.
quote: Modular and type-safe form library for SolidJS, Preact, React, Svelte, Vue and Qwik

claim: HN: a two-person SaaS with 'a lot of highly dynamic forms and fairly complex client side state' shipped on Next.js + oRPC + Zod + TanStack Form + TanStack Query + Drizzle — a real production data point for TanStack Form on form-heavy apps.
quote: it involves a lot of highly dynamic forms and fairly complex client side state ... The stack ... Nextjs, oRPC, Next-Intl, Zod, Tanstack Form, Tanstack Query, Drizzle, SQLite, Tiptap, Better-Auth, Jest, Tailwind, a heavily customized Shadcn.

claim: OpenAI's Codex desktop app (Electron) ships TanStack React Form alongside React 19, Jotai and Zod — evidence of TanStack Form in a shipped, high-visibility product.
quote: Here's the Codex tech stack... Frontend:- React 19.2.0- Jotai (state management)- TanStack React Form- Vite (bundler)- TypeScript

claim: TanStack Form consumes Standard Schema natively with no adapter/resolver package, covering Zod, Valibot, ArkType and Effect/Schema.
quote: TanStack Form natively supports all libraries following the [Standard Schema specification](https://github.com/standard-schema/standard-schema), most notably: Zod, Valibot, ArkType, Effect/Schema ... _Note:_ make sure to use the latest version of the schema libraries as older versions might not support Standard Schema yet.

claim: TanStack Form ships dedicated meta-framework packages (@tanstack/react-form-nextjs, -start, -remix) exposing createServerValidate/ServerValidateError/initialFormState/mergeForm/useTransform; the Next.js path wires straight into React 19 useActionState.
quote: Today we support the following meta-frameworks: TanStack Start, Next.js, Remix ... const [state, action] = useActionState(someAction, initialFormState) ... transform: useTransform((baseForm) => mergeForm(baseForm, state!), [state])

claim: @hookform/resolvers 5.4.0 (published 2026-05-21) exposes a './standard-schema' export alongside './zod', './valibot', './arktype', './yup', and peer-depends on react-hook-form ^7.55.0.
quote: exports: ['./zod', './yup', './arktype', './valibot', './standard-schema'] ; peerDependencies: {'react-hook-form': '^7.55.0'}

claim: React Hook Form has no official maintainer position on React 19 Server Actions / useActionState: the 'React v19 Discussion' thread (opened April 2024) is still marked Unanswered as of 2026, with only community workarounds.
quote: Should react-hook-form keep their current state management strategy, or integrate with React's new APIs? ... [thread remains marked "Unanswered"]

claim: React Hook Form's progressive-enhancement story is its own <Form /> component plus useForm({ progressive: true }) which emits native action/method attributes and POSTs to a URL endpoint - not React 19 Server Functions.
quote: Progressively enhancement for your form. ... <Form action="/api" method="post" onSubmit={()=>{}} onSuccess={()=>{}} onError={()=>{}} validateStatus={(status)=>status>=200} /> ... Progressive Enhancement only applicable for SSR framework. const { handleSubmit, control } = useForm({ progressive: true });

claim: Combining React Hook Form with useActionState in the Next.js App Router requires a hack (a timestamp field) because the form clears itself on repeated submissions with unchanged data.
quote: making react-hook-form work with the latest React 19 and Next.js 15 releases feels a bit hacky, mainly because we need a workaround to make it work when submitting a form two or multiple times.

claim: Conform's 'future' useForm export (the de-facto v2) drops duplicated form state, uses the DOM as source of truth, and takes any Standard Schema directly on useForm.
quote: Conform already uses the DOM as the source of truth. Why are we duplicating all this state in React? ... Simply pass your schema to `useForm` and it will handle parsing and validation for you.

claim: Formisch is a new (2025-2026) schema-first, signal-based, headless form library by Fabian Hiller (author of Valibot and co-author of Standard Schema), supporting React, Vue, Solid, Svelte, Preact and Qwik from one core.
quote: The lightweight, schema-first, and fully type-safe form library for React, Solid, Vue, Svelte and more

claim: Formisch reached 1.0 Release Candidate in mid-2026; it is Valibot-only (Valibot is the sole source of truth for validation AND types), bundles from ~2.5 kB, and its RC announcement says nothing about SSR/server actions.
quote: you describe your form once with a Valibot schema ... the bundle size starts at around 2.5 kB ... Formisch runs on React, Vue, Solid, Qwik, Svelte, and Preact from a single core.

claim: Standard Schema is a common interface spec for TypeScript validation libraries; the spec site publishes the interface (@standard-schema/spec on npm/JSR) for libraries to implement and for consumers (e.g. form libraries) to accept.
quote: Libraries wishing to implement a spec can copy/paste the code block
